fields.name: Udayagiri–Khandagiri Caves
fields.short_description: Udayagiri and Khandagiri are ancient rock-cut cave complexes near Bhubaneswar, known for their historical inscriptions, sculptures, Jain heritage, and remarkable rock-cut architecture.
fields.culture_description:
Udayagiri and Khandagiri are ancient rock-cut cave complexes near Bhubaneswar that represent an important part of Odisha's early Jain heritage.

The caves were carved into natural hills and were used by Jain ascetics. Many of them contain inscriptions, sculptural panels, decorative carvings, and architectural features that provide insight into the religious and cultural life of ancient Odisha.

The complex is especially known for its historic caves, rock-cut chambers, and detailed stone carvings, making it an important archaeological and cultural landmark.
fields.food_description:
The food traditions around Udayagiri–Khandagiri reflect the authentic flavours of Odisha.

Traditional Meals:
Rice, dal, seasonal vegetables and traditional Odia curries form an important part of everyday meals.

Dalma:
Dalma is a traditional Odia dish prepared with lentils and vegetables, seasoned with aromatic spices.

Pakhala:
Pakhala is a popular rice-based dish especially enjoyed during Odisha's warmer months and is commonly served with vegetables and traditional side dishes.

Traditional Sweets:
Chhena Poda, Rasabali and other traditional Odia sweets represent the rich culinary heritage of the region.

fields.name: Shree Jagannath Temple, Puri
fields.short_description: Shree Jagannath Temple in Puri is one of Odisha's most significant religious and cultural landmarks. Dedicated to Lord Jagannath, the temple is deeply connected with Odisha's traditions, festivals, art, cuisine and cultural identity.
fields.culture_description:
Shree Jagannath Temple is one of Odisha's most important religious and cultural landmarks and is deeply connected with the identity and traditions of Puri.

Jagannath culture centres around Lord Jagannath, along with Lord Balabhadra and Devi Subhadra. The temple preserves centuries-old rituals, festivals, traditional art, music and community practices.

The annual Rath Yatra is one of its most celebrated traditions, during which the three deities travel in magnificent wooden chariots. Jagannath culture has also influenced Odisha's literature, painting, dance, food traditions and everyday cultural life.
fields.food_description:
Mahaprasad is an important part of the religious and cultural traditions associated with Shree Jagannath Temple.

Temple Cuisine:
Traditional food is prepared as an offering to the deities following established temple customs and cooking practices.

Mahaprasad:
After being offered to the deities, the sacred food is known as Mahaprasad. It is shared among devotees and represents devotion, community and equality.

Traditional Preparation:
The temple kitchen is famous for its traditional cooking practices, including the use of earthen pots. Rice, dal, vegetables, sweets and other preparations form part of the temple food tradition.

Cultural Significance:
Mahaprasad is more than food; it forms an important part of Jagannath culture and Odisha's living culinary heritage.

fields.name: Konark Sun Temple
fields.short_description: The Konark Sun Temple is a historic temple renowned for its monumental stone architecture and intricate carvings.
fields.culture_description: Konark is a historic coastal town in the Puri district of Odisha, India, globally renowned for its 13th-century Sun Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The town's name originates from the Sanskrit words Kona (corner) and Arka (sun), literally translating to the "Corner of the Sun". Together with Bhubaneswar and Puri, Konark forms the "Golden Triangle" of Odisha tourism.
fields.food_description:
Puri–Konark cuisine is a blend of sacred temple food and traditional coastal flavours.

Sacred Temple Food:
Rice, dal, vegetables, and traditional dishes are prepared using simple ingredients and age-old cooking methods. Temple cuisine traditionally avoids onion and garlic.

Coastal Cuisine:
The coastal region is known for fresh fish, prawns, and crab dishes, often prepared with mustard, coconut, and traditional spices.

Sweet Heritage:
Popular Odia sweets include Chhena Poda, Khaja, and other milk-based delicacies that form an important part of the region's culinary heritage.

Flavour Profile:
The cuisine is simple, aromatic, and earthy, commonly using mustard oil, panch phoron (five-spice blend), and fresh coconut.

fields.name: Raghurajpur Heritage Village
fields.short_description: Raghurajpur is a traditional heritage crafts village in Odisha, renowned for its Pattachitra paintings, palm-leaf art, traditional crafts, and rich cultural traditions.
fields.culture_description:
Raghurajpur is a heritage crafts village in Odisha known for preserving traditional art forms through generations of artisan families.

The village is especially famous for Pattachitra, a traditional painting style created on prepared cloth using natural colours and intricate decorative patterns.

Artists of Raghurajpur also practise palm-leaf engraving, traditional mask making, wooden crafts and other forms of Odisha folk art. The village represents a living cultural ecosystem where traditional knowledge, craftsmanship and everyday community life remain closely connected.
fields.food_description:
Raghurajpur's food traditions reflect the simple and authentic flavours of rural Odisha.

Traditional Meals:
Daily meals commonly include rice, dal, seasonal vegetables and traditional Odia preparations made with locally available ingredients.

Pakhala:
Pakhala, prepared from cooked rice soaked in water, is a popular traditional dish especially enjoyed during the summer months. It is commonly served with vegetables and other side dishes.

Traditional Sweets:
Odia sweets such as Khaja, Chhena Poda and other locally prepared delicacies are part of the region's culinary tradition.

Food Heritage:
The cuisine represents Odisha's traditional village lifestyle, where simple ingredients, seasonal produce and generations-old cooking practices remain important.

fields.description: Konark Sun Temple was built in the 13th century during the reign of King Narasimhadeva I.

Today, the Konark Sun Temple stands as one of Odisha's most
important preserved heritage monuments. Although parts of the
original structure have been lost over time, conservation efforts
continue to protect its architecture, sculptures, and cultural legacy.

Raghurajpur developed as a traditional artisan village where generations of families practised and preserved Odisha's indigenous art forms. Pattachitra painting, palm-leaf engraving, mask making and other crafts became deeply connected with the everyday life and cultural identity of the village.

Today, Raghurajpur continues to thrive as a living heritage village where traditional art and everyday community life exist together. Artisan families continue to practise Pattachitra painting, palm-leaf engraving, mask making and other traditional crafts while sharing these cultural traditions with visitors and future generations.

During the ancient Kalinga period, the Udayagiri and Khandagiri hills developed as important centres associated with Jain ascetics. Rock-cut caves, inscriptions, sculptures and chambers created in the hills reflect the religious, artistic and architectural traditions of ancient Odisha.

Today, the Udayagiri and Khandagiri Caves remain important archaeological and cultural landmarks of Odisha. Their rock-cut chambers, inscriptions, sculptures and Jain heritage continue to provide visitors with a glimpse into the region's ancient history while preservation efforts help protect the site for future generations.

During the Eastern Ganga dynasty, the great temple at Puri developed into an important centre of worship and cultural life. The temple became closely associated with Lord Jagannath and traditions that would deeply influence Odisha's religious, artistic and cultural identity.

Today, Shree Jagannath Temple remains one of Odisha's most important religious and cultural centres. Centuries-old rituals, festivals, Mahaprasad traditions and the annual Rath Yatra continue to keep Jagannath culture alive while connecting generations of devotees with Odisha's living heritage.

Nuakhai
fields.description: Nuakhai is an important agricultural festival celebrated in Western Odisha to welcome the new rice harvest.
fields.cultural_significance: The festival expresses gratitude for the new harvest and celebrates community, family, tradition, and prosperity.
fields.practices: People prepare the new rice, offer it to the deities, wear traditional clothes, visit relatives, exchange greetings, and celebrate together with traditional food and cultural activities.

fields.title: Manabasa Gurubara Puja
fields.description: Manabasa Gurubara is a traditional Odia puja dedicated to Goddess Lakshmi and is especially observed by women in Odisha during the month of Margashira.
fields.cultural_significance: The puja is associated with prosperity, cleanliness, devotion, family well-being, and the worship of Goddess Lakshmi.
fields.practices: Homes are cleaned and decorated with beautiful Jhoti and Chita designs, devotees prepare traditional offerings, and Goddess Lakshmi is worshipped with prayers and rituals on Thursdays.

fields.title: Rath Yatra
fields.description: Rath Yatra is a major annual festival in Odisha in which the deities of the Jagannath Temple are taken in grand chariots through the streets of Puri.
fields.cultural_significance: The festival represents devotion, community participation, and the tradition of Lord Jagannath and the sacred culture of Puri.
fields.practices: Devotees gather in large numbers, participate in the chariot procession, offer prayers, and celebrate with devotional songs and traditional activities.

fields.title: Raja Parba
fields.description: Raja Parba is a traditional festival of Odisha that celebrates womanhood, fertility, and the arrival of the monsoon.
fields.cultural_significance: The festival honors Mother Earth and celebrates womanhood, fertility, nature, and the beginning of the rainy season.
fields.practices: People(especially girls) wear new clothes, enjoy traditional swings, prepare special foods such as Poda Pitha, visit family and friends, and take part in festive activities.
